transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-20
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Solstice Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Solstice PM), Ethan Lowe (Solstice SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on the incremental KV warmup pilot. Review of latest hit-rate numbers, discussion of prefetch cohort strategy, tuning eviction and TTLs, and planning a short live-traffic replay benchmark. Decided on an action plan for a small staged rollout and a targeted benchmark next week.

Topics:
- Current KV/prefix hit rate trends
- Prefetch cohort selection and whitelist
- Eviction policies & TTL tuning
- Tradeoffs: latency overhead vs token cost
- Next steps: benchmarks, configs, access

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, we are on for about 45 minutes so we can go through the week-over-week numbers and then Maya will walk through the incremental warmup configs we've been testing. Jordan, Priya, Ethan, you good on time?
[00:12] Jordan (Solstice): Yep all good, thanks. Quick heads up, Ethan needs to step out at the 35 minute mark for a incident, but we'll try to stay intact.
[00:20] Alex: Totally fine. Maya, over to you.
[00:22] Maya (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll share my screen in a sec. So last week we shipped the smaller prefetch window and increased cohort granularity — what we saw was overall KV hit-rate bumped from ~18% to ~26% on staging for the 0-512 token prompts. But there is some churn on the long-tail users.
[00:40] Jordan: When you say cohort granularity can you unpack that — is that user-id based or context type?
[00:45] Maya: Good question. Right now the pilot uses session-id + intent-hash to pick a cohort, so it's a mix. We added a second level that groups by the last 3 prompt tokens pattern which seems to catch repeated instruction formats.
[00:58] Priya: Are we seeing regression on latency when we prefetch more aggressively?
[01:02] Maya: Minimal — median latency increased ~12ms, p95 up ~40ms on staging with the larger prefetch window. There's a cost bump on tokens served since prefetch generates extra requests, so we wanted to discuss thresholds where the hit-rate benefit offsets the token cost.
[01:18] Alex: And to be explicit, the target is to keep user-facing tail latency within 200ms for our b2b use-case, right? Jordan, is that what you are measuring?
[01:27] Jordan: We're using the app SLO which is 250ms p95 so we have a bit of headroom. The concern is unpredictable spikes when the KV cache evicts a hot prefix during bursts.
[01:38] Maya: On evictions we saw that LRU with a small TTL causes oscillation for a subset of high-frequency queries. We prototyped a hybrid eviction (LRU + frequency decay) and it reduced thrash in the monitored cohort.
[01:52] Ethan (SRE): Can you say a little more about the frequency decay? Sounds like LFU?
[01:55] Maya: It's similar to LFU but with an exponential decay over a rolling window so older hits lose weight; that stabilizes when traffic pattern shifts. Implementation is lightweight in the runtime.
[02:05] Jordan: Our traffic has diurnal spikes and also sudden jumps from sync jobs, so decay helps. But we need to be careful about cold-start for new users — prefetch should not waste tokens for essentially one-off queries.
[02:17] Priya: Right — we were thinking of a whitelist of prefixes derived from product telemetry. Is Redwood comfortable shipping a whitelist for the pilot?
[02:25] Maya: Yes — we can share a recommended whitelist. We're also testing a small heuristics module that picks prefixes by recent frequency + conversion signal.
[02:35] Alex: To be clear on metrics, the primary metric for this pilot is net token cost per successful cache hit and secondary is p95 latency. Maya, can you share the raw hit-rate CSV?
[02:44] Maya: Yep I'll send the CSV after the call. Quick callout: one anomaly — there's a customer's integration that sends large system prompts, which fragment the prefix and lowers hit rate. The transcription in the logs reads as weird tokens cause, um, prefix splitting — so might be an integration fix on your side.
[03:02] Jordan: That might be us; our client library was adding a timestamp string in the system prompt. We'll dig in.
[03:08] Ethan: We can strip that at ingestion if that's the issue.
[03:11] Alex: Great.
[03:12] [03:12] Maya: Next, the incremental warmup approach: rather than prefetching full context for all new sessions we warm prefixes in phases — phase 0 prefetch most-likely 1-2 tokens, phase 1 expand to 8-16 tokens, phase 2 full contextual window for heavy cohorts. This reduces wasted token overhead for short-lived sessions.
[03:35] Jordan: Do you gate phases on observed hit-rate or on session age?
[03:39] Maya: We gate on session age + a small lookback for repeated prompts. If a session issues >3 similar prompts in a 10-min window we escalate phase.
[03:47] Priya: That seems reasonable. What's the expected token overhead delta?
[03:50] Maya: In our sim it was +6% tokens overall but hit-rate improved enough in the high-value cohort to give net savings — YMMV depending on your ratio of long vs short sessions.
[04:02] Jordan: Can you show the cohort heatmap?
[04:05] Maya: (screen share) Here's a heatmap — rows are cohorts, columns week-over-week. See cohort 14 had a big jump after we tuned the prefetch window. But cohort 21 remains low — that's where we think the long system prompts are fragmenting.
[04:22] Jordan: OK that maps. For cohort selection we may want to align with our product cohorts (by tenant) rather than algorithmic clusters — we have tenants that are low-volume but high-importance.
[04:34] Alex: We can support tenant-aware cohorts; that may actually be simpler for policy rollouts.
[04:39] Priya: About rollout — what's the recommended ramp? 5% -> 20% -> 50%?
[04:44] Maya: We recommend three-step ramp: 2% -> 15% -> 50% with monitoring gates at each step for cost and latency deltas. For tenants with stricter SLOs do canary only.
[04:56] Ethan: For the monitoring gates, what logs/metrics do you need from our side for the benchmark?
[05:00] Maya: Token-level per-request latency, per-request KV hit boolean, eviction events, and a small sample of prefetch payloads. If you can send those in a structured log or a S3 dump that's ideal.
[05:11] Ethan: We can add structured fields, yes. We'll patch staging for the replay.
[05:15] Alex: One enterprise topic — security/data residency. Priya raised this last week: prefetching stores prefix snapshots in the KV store. Are there concerns about PII or PHI given Solstice is in healthcare?
[05:27] Priya: Yeah we have strict controls; we need to be sure prefetch store is encrypted at rest and access logged. Also we prefer not to store full-turn user content unless it's anonymized.
[05:36] Maya: Understood. For the pilot we configure prefix hashes and store only hashed tokens + minimal metadata. All stored artifacts in our private deployment are encrypted with customer-managed KMS as an option; we can toggle that for this pilot.
[05:49] Jordan: Can Redwood provide the short security checklist for the prefetch data handling? That will help our compliance team.
[05:54] Alex: We'll send the short checklist and relevant SOC2 excerpts.
[05:58] Priya: Cool. Also one thing about burst behavior — when you prefetch you create background requests; how do you prevent amplification where background warms consume capacity and cause evictions?
[06:07] Maya: We set a soft budget for prefetch QPS per node and throttle prefetch during high CPU/GPU load. The runtime respects capacity reservations and has a fallback to on-demand if budgets are exceeded.
[06:18] Ethan: We'll want to test that in the replay; can you simulate throttling?
[06:22] Maya: Yes, Maya: we have a simulated throttle mode that slows prefetch to a configurable QPS and reports back. We'll provide config for that.
[06:31] Alex: Ok, let's go through the immediate numbers again — Jordan you sent a CSV with 72 hours of staging traffic, any highlights?
[06:38] Jordan: Right, quick highlights: baseline hit-rate 18% median; after the smaller prefetch window we saw 26% on staging; cost per 1k requests increased ~8% but token savings in the targeted cohort reduced overall net cost by ~3% in that slice. The long-tail still hurts us — about 30% of sessions generate 60% of wasted prefetch tokens.
[06:56] Maya: That long-tail is usually botty traffic or background syncs; metadata-based filtering reduces noise.
[07:03] Priya: We can add a filter at ingestion that marks known background jobs; not all are obvious.
[07:09] Jordan: We'll add a flag in the sampling harness to label traffic types.
[07:13] [07:13] Alex: Good. Next, checklist for benchmark: Redwood to provide perf spreadsheet + runbook; Solstice to run replay with a configured replay window and provide logs; then joint analysis. Any scheduling constraints?
[07:25] Ethan: The best window is Wed-Fri next week (2027-05-31 to 2027-06-02) when our staging traffic is a good mimic.
[07:33] Maya: Works for us — we'll hold the week open for a 30-min checkpoint after the first day.
[07:38] Priya: About cost reporting — we need a clear metric: net token cost delta normalized by successful cached responses.
[07:46] Maya: We can compute "token-cost-per-hit" and send that in the spreadsheet.
[07:50] Jordan: One more runtime question: do you support pinning prefix TTL per-tenant?
[07:55] Maya: Yes, TTLs are configurable at tenant or cohort level in the control plane.
[07:59] Ethan: We'll probably set conservative TTLs for our sensitive tenants.
[08:03] Alex: Anything else on risks or open items?
[08:05] Priya: Need that security checklist and KMS options; also a short runbook in case prefetch causes spike evictions.
[08:12] Alex: We'll include a rollback toggle and eviction debug logs in the runbook.
[08:16] Jordan: Cool.
[08:18] [08:18] Alex: Alright, quick recap of action items — I'll list them and then we can close.
[08:22] Alex: Alex — send perf spreadsheet, CSV, security checklist (due 2027-05-24). Maya — incremental warmup config + simulated throttle mode (due 2027-05-24). Jordan — deploy sampling harness to staging and run the 72 hour capture and share logs (due 2027-05-27). Ethan — set up replay window and grant access for benchmark (due 2027-05-28).
[08:38] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks team.
[08:42] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and a short checkpoint after day 1.
[08:50] Jordan: Bye all.

End of transcript.
